question: Can a simple generic retrieval augmented LM decide actively when and what to retrieve during long-form generation, instead of retrieving once from the input?
hypothesis: LMs should retrieve only when they lack knowledge (low-probability tokens), and queries should reflect the intent of future generation rather than past context.
contributions: A generalized framework of active retrieval augmented generation that decides when and what to retrieve across generation
FLARE (instruct and direct variants), which uses the upcoming sentence as a query when it contains low-confidence tokens
Evaluation on 4 long-form knowledge-intensive tasks against single-time and multi-time retrieval baselines

method.summary: FLARE drafts the next sentence without retrieval, and if any token has probability below theta, uses the draft (masked or turned into questions) as a retrieval query and regenerates the sentence with the retrieved documents. It is applied at inference time to text-davinci-003 with few-shot prompts, with no training.
method.task: long-form knowledge-intensive generation: multihop QA, commonsense QA, long-form QA, open-domain summarization

datasets.name: 2WikiMultihopQA
datasets.preprocessing: chain-of-thought and final answer generated; answer extracted by regex

datasets.name: ASQA-hint
datasets.source: ASQA with a brief ambiguity hint added by the authors

datasets.name: WikiAsp
datasets.preprocessing: converted to open-domain by removing references; retrieval from the open web; Wikipedia-related domains excluded from Bing results (wikipedia.org, wikiwand.com, wiki2.org, wikimedia.org)

other.note: input length limit limits 2WikiMultihopQA to 2 retrieved documents

other.use: zero-shot question generation for explicit queries

models.name: BM25
models.architecture: sparse lexical retriever over Wikipedia dump from Karpukhin et al. (2020)

models.name: Bing search API
models.architecture: web search engine, used for WikiAsp

inference.max_tokens: 64 tokens generated per step, first sentence kept via NLTK Punkt sentence tokenizer, rest discarded
inference.prompting: few-shot in-context: 8 exemplars (2WikiMultihopQA), 6 (StrategyQA), 8 (ASQA and ASQA-hint), 4 (WikiAsp); retrieved docs prepended before user input via Prompt D.1
inference.retrieval: Top-k docs: 2 (2WikiMultihopQA), 3 (StrategyQA), 3 (ASQA, ASQA-hint), 5 (WikiAsp). Only the current step's documents are kept. First sentence uses the user input as the initial query. Exemplars on 2WikiMultihopQA also get retrieved docs.

parameters.theta (retrieval trigger threshold): 0.8 for 2WikiMultihopQA, ASQA, ASQA-hint, WikiAsp; 0.4 for StrategyQA
parameters.query formulation: implicit (masking) for 2WikiMultihopQA and StrategyQA; explicit (question generation) for ASQA, ASQA-hint, WikiAsp
parameters.combine single- and multi-time retrieval: yes for ASQA, ASQA-hint, WikiAsp; no for 2WikiMultihopQA, StrategyQA
parameters.FLARE-instruct: logit of token '[' increased by 2.0; after a query the query is removed and next tokens generated with '[' forbidden by a large negative logit

other.hyperparameter selection: selected on the development set (dev size not stated)

metrics.name: EM
metrics.definition: exact match of extracted final answer with reference (ASQA: EM from Stelmakh et al.)

metrics.name: DR
metrics.definition: overall score combining Disambig-F1 and ROUGE

eval.protocol: Single run on sub-sampled sets of at most 500 examples; no seeds or significance tests reported. Baselines are re-implementations under the same settings, not exact reproductions.

results.claim: FLARE-direct reaches 51.0 EM on 2WikiMultihopQA, above single-time retrieval (39.4) and question decomposition (47.8).
results.setup: 2WikiMultihopQA, text-davinci-003, BM25 top-2 Wikipedia, 8 exemplars, theta 0.8 beta 0.4 implicit
results.note: single-time 39.4, question decomposition 47.8, no retrieval 28.2, previous-window 43.2, previous-sentence 39.0

results.claim: FLARE-instruct reaches only 42.4 EM on 2WikiMultihopQA, far below FLARE-direct.
On StrategyQA FLARE gets 77.3 EM, while single-time retrieval (68.6) is worse than no retrieval (72.9).
results.setup: StrategyQA, text-davinci-003, BM25 top-3, 6 exemplars, theta 0.4

results.claim: On ASQA-hint FLARE gets 46.2 EM versus 43.2 for single-time retrieval.
results.setup: ASQA-hint, text-davinci-003, BM25 top-3, explicit queries

results.claim: On ASQA FLARE gets 41.3 EM versus 40.0 single-time; gain is small.
On WikiAsp FLARE gets 53.4 UniEval versus 52.4 single-time.
Retrieving with the next sentence beats the previous sentence on 2WikiMultihopQA (48.8 vs 39.0 EM).
results.setup: 2WikiMultihopQA, retrieve every sentence with full previous or next sentence as query

results.claim: Previous-window baseline degrades when more past tokens are used as query (16 tokens 43.2 EM, all 39.0 EM).
Masking low-confidence tokens helps: beta 0.4 gives 0.510 EM versus 0.488 at beta 0 (full sentence).
Implicit and explicit query formulation perform similarly on ASQA-hint (45.7 vs 46.2 EM).
Triggering retrieval for 40%-80% of sentences usually performs well; on StrategyQA performance drops above 50% retrieval.
results.setup: theta sweep on 2WikiMultihopQA and StrategyQA, Fig 5
results.quote: We found triggering retrieval for 40%-80% of sentences usually leads to a good per-formance across tasks/datasets.
results.note: quote has an extraction hyphenation artifact

limits: No significant gain on Wizard of Wikipedia (short outputs, about 20 tokens) or ELI5 (grounding and evaluation issues).
Naive interleaving increases overhead and cost; LM called once per retrieval and activations recomputed without caching.
Tested only on text-davinci-003 (API snapshot of April 23), at most 500 examples per dataset, single runs without significance tests.
Baselines are re-implementations, not exact reproductions; FLARE-instruct needed logit hacks and underperformed.
Gains on ASQA and WikiAsp are about 1 point.

terms.definition: a framework that actively decides when and what to retrieve through the generation process, interleaving retrieval and generation
Forward-Looking Active REtrieval augmented generation: iteratively uses a prediction of the upcoming sentence as the query, retrieving and regenerating if it contains low-confidence tokens

lineage.note: previous-sentence baseline; exemplars for 2WikiMultihopQA taken from it
